subject: Tranche-hedge MAP: evaluation sprint + capacity handoff (Dedicated & Private)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tranche-hedge MAP: evaluation sprint + capacity handoff (Dedicated & Private)

Tom —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Per our conversation I sketched a tranche-hedge Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on minimizing your procurement risk while keeping the proof-of-value (PoV) fast. High level:

- Goal: run a 3-4 week eval with production-like traffic, land commit decision within 6–8 weeks of start.
- Primary constraints: SOC2 scoping confirmation; VPC-only access for PHI; procurement decision gate by Oct 1.
- Capacity hedge: start with a small reserved pool (4 x A100-equivalent) for the PoV and then ramp to a full tranche (target 20 GPUs) within 8–10 weeks post-commit.

Lead time assumptions (please confirm):
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool): typical procurement + provisioning = 10–14 weeks after contract signature (hardware tranche allocation + networking).
- Redwood Private (VPC on customer cloud / on-prem): provisioning 8–12 weeks (depends on cloud approvals and VPC peering schedule).

What we need from Nexa to finalize MAP and the sizing worksheet:
1) Expected peak concurrent requests (p95 QPS) for your 1.0 model and 1.1 variant.
2) Latency SLO targets (p95/token or p95/response).
3) Allowed quantization (if any) and whether 8-bit / 4-bit is acceptable for the PoV.
4) SOC2 evidence owner + procurement contact for contract timing.

I attached a draft MAP and a preliminary GPU sizing sheet for your team to fill. Suggested next steps:
- You: confirm the procurement contact + basic workload numbers (items 1–3) by EOD Thu 8/12
- Us: we’ll lock a PO-ready tranche plan and propose a staggered rollout with canary (2-week) and 2x fallback capacity to avoid cold-start pressure.

If that schedule works I’ll book a 30-minute handshake to walk the MAP and the acceptance gates.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

Attachments: nexa_map_draft.pdf (MAP outline), gpu-sizing-sheet.xlsx (worksheet)

Mina —

Thanks, this looks sensible. High level responses:

- We can start the PoV the week of Aug 24 (internal approvals permitting). Expect 3 full weeks of active testing.
- Peak concurrently: ~120 p95 requests/minute for the main model (estimating 1.2k tokens per response average); variant traffic ~20% of that.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end <800ms for the interactive flow; batch jobs can be higher.
- Quantization: internal ML team is comfortable with 8-bit quant for now; won’t accept 4-bit without more eval.
- SOC2: I’ve looped procurement — they own the contract schedule (cc’d). They are tracking DocuSign approvals and will share standard terms.

Procurement note: procurement asked whether we can propose a staged billing approach to align with tranche delivery. I’m attaching a quick procurement window spreadsheet.

I’ll have procurement confirm the contract owner and a target Oct 1 decision date by EOD Wed 8/12.

Tom

Tom.Rivera@nexahealth.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tranche-hedge MAP: evaluation sprint + capacity handoff (Dedicated & Private)

Tom / Mina —

Good context — thanks. A few pragmatic notes from an operations + sizing perspective so the MAP has concrete acceptance gates and a mitigation plan.

Sizing assumptions I used in the attached GPU worksheet (column notes):
- Baseline inference mix: 80% chat-style sessions (avg 1.2k tokens), 20% batch/rerank.
- Realistic throughput per A100-like GPU (fp16, batching): ~450–700 qps depending on batching and model length. For safety used 500 qps per GPU at target latency.
- For the PoV: reserve 4 GPUs (hedge tranche) — supports ~2k qps peak which gives room for variance and tracing.
- For production: target 20 GPUs (tranche 1) which supports ~10k qps with continued batching and prefix caching.

Operational mitigations (MAP clauses to include):
- Canary window: 48–72 hours with synthetic load + traffic shadowing. Acceptance gate: p95 latency within 1.25x of the SLO and error rate <0.3%.
- Auto-scale buffer: 15% standby capacity available for burst; if sustained >20% above baseline for >30 minutes, trigger tranche escalation.
- Fallback model: when Dedicated capacity is constrained we’ll automatically route low-priority traffic to Hosted LLM variant with rate-limited fallthrough to preserve critical production flows.

Lead-time & procurement notes (practical):
- If contract signed by Sep 1, Dedicated tranche provisioning typically completes by mid-Nov; Private (cloud/VPC) can often be faster if customer cloud approvals are in place (~8 weeks).
- To shorten calendar risk, we recommend a staged acceptance: sign SOW for PoV + preliminary tranche deposit (non-refundable credit) to secure the 4-GPU hedge pool while full procurement completes. That reduces your exposure and locks capacity.

I’ve updated the GPU sizing sheet with the conservative numbers and added a short checklist for the PoV acceptance tests. See attached gpu-sizing-sheet.xlsx.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Tom: confirm peak p95 numbers and SOC2 evidence owner by Thu 8/12 (customer).
- Procurement (Nexa): confirm preferred billing cadence and DocuSign approver by Wed 8/12.
- Mina: prepare a short SOW + deposit invoice for the 4-GPU hedge tranche by Fri 8/14 (Redwood).
- Soojin: prepare canary runbook and acceptance checklist by Fri 8/14 (Redwood).

If everyone agrees I’ll include the staged deposit language in the MAP and we can get the PoV SOW signed this week — that materially reduces the 10–14 week risk window.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
